## AC7 — Item 10 census ("Parser of record"), read-only, no files edited

Measured on `origin/main` at `38c42c7e70e`. **13 files, 1 occurrence each, 0 duplicates.**

| File:line | Result |
|---|---|
| `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:227` | DISCARDED |
| `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py:149` | DISCARDED |
| `src/rebar/_commands/attach_commits.py:25` | DISCARDED |
| `src/rebar/_commands/delete.py:263` | DISCARDED |
| `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py:450` | DISCARDED |
| `src/rebar/_commands/init.py:605` | DISCARDED |
| `src/rebar/_commands/scratch.py:235` | DISCARDED |
| `src/rebar/_commands/unlink.py:297` | DISCARDED |
| `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:427` | USED — `try/except ParseError` |
| `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_recover.py:158` | USED — `try/except ParseError` |
| `src/rebar/_commands/link_revert.py:421` | USED — `try/except ParseError` |
| `src/rebar/_commands/session_log.py:272` | USED — `try/except ParseError` |
| `src/rebar/_commands/tracker_maintenance.py:177` | USED — `try/except ParseError` |

**8 DISCARDED, 5 USED.** The 5 USED sites discard the `Namespace` but do catch and render a
`ParseError`, so the parser is load-bearing as a *rejecter* there and those sites are not dead
code.

**Discrepancy resolved: 13 is correct.** The earlier figures of 21 and 14 are both wrong. The
count was verified independently three times on the live tree — by the implementing agent twice
(file-level `grep -rln` and occurrence-level `grep -rc`), and once more during close review
(`grep -rln` = 13 files, `grep -rn` = 13 occurrences). The USED/DISCARDED split was
independently confirmed at close review by a `ParseError` census: each of the 5 USED files
carries exactly 2 `ParseError` references (the raise/catch pair); the sampled DISCARDED files
(`delete.py`, `attach_commits.py`, `unlink.py`) carry 0. Case-sensitivity is not the cause of
the gap — `[Pp]arser of record` finds 3 additional files, but those use the phrase lowercase
mid-sentence rather than as the capitalized marker-comment header, and 16 reconciles with
neither 21 nor 14.

## AC8 — Item 3's two further cross-references

**(a) `set_relationship` / `payload["links"]` — DANGLING, fixed.**
Site: `src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_pass.py:167-172`. Old text claimed
`_apply_outbound_update` itself *"reads `payload["links"]` and calls
`client.set_relationship`"*. It does neither directly. Verified at close review against
`apply_outbound.py:129`, whose own docstring reads *"Outbound update — delegate to the ONE
production applier (batch `update_one`)"*; the `payload["links"]` read and the
`client.set_relationship` call happen in `update_one`'s link-dispatch phase in
`dispatch_apply_phases.py`. Corrected text now names that delegation chain.

**(b) Re-export claims — SOUND, no edits.**
Three re-export blocks in `src/rebar/reconciler/applier.py`:

- ~98-99, from `apply_inbound.py` — all 6 named symbols (`_apply_inbound_clean_label`,
  `_apply_inbound_conflict`, `_apply_inbound_create`, `_apply_inbound_repair_property`,
  `_apply_inbound_update`, `inbound_repair_property`) are `def`-ed there. SOUND.
- ~108-110, from `apply_outbound.py` — all 7 named symbols (`_apply_outbound_conflict`,
  `_apply_outbound_create`, `_apply_outbound_delete`, `_apply_outbound_probe`,
  `_apply_outbound_update`, `_drift_is_benign`, `_get_commit_subject`) are `def`-ed there. SOUND.
- ~120-121, from `batch_dispatch.py` — `JiraAPIError` is *defined* in
  `src/rebar/reconciler/_errors.py:64`, then imported and re-exported (with an `__all__` entry)
  by `batch_dispatch.py`. The comment's "lives in batch_dispatch.py" names the exposing module
  in a multi-hop re-export chain rather than the literal def site, and the import resolves.
  SOUND — a chain, not a dangling reference.

All 13 symbols in the first two blocks were re-verified to resolve at close review.

## AC9 — Item 9 (`floors.py`) is not a behavioural bug

Both appliers only ever move findings between `verdict["advisory"]` and `verdict["dropped"]`
and never touch `verdict["blocking"]`, so omitting `decide._recompute_verdict_after_drop`
cannot change the PASS/BLOCK outcome. Recorded as a docstring note on both appliers rather than
reported as a separate bug.
